remote_work_stipend: Employees approved for remote work may claim up to $500 USD per calendar year for home office equipment, ergonomic accessories, and approved connectivity costs. Claims require an itemized receipt and manager approval before reimbursement.
remote_work_stipend_expenses: Eligible stipend expenses include desks, chairs, external monitors, webcams, headsets, docking stations, and a one-time internet upgrade fee. Ineligible expenses include rent, utilities, personal entertainment, and general household items unrelated to work.
remote_work_stipend_deadline: Stipend reimbursement requests must be submitted within 45 days of the purchase date. Requests submitted after the deadline require Finance review and may be denied.
it_security_password_rules: Corporate passwords must be at least 14 characters long and include a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Passwords may not contain the user's name, email address, or company name.
it_security_password_rotation: Passwords must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected. Routine password rotation is not required unless a privileged account is flagged by Security or an incident response ticket is opened.
it_security_mfa: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for VPN access, email, payroll, source control, and any application that stores customer or employee data. Approved MFA methods are authenticator apps and hardware security keys.
mess_management_system: The Mess Management System is an internal enterprise platform used for meal planning, vendor coordination, and cafeteria reporting across regional offices.
mess_management_system_deployment_stack: The Mess Management System deployment stack uses React for the frontend, FastAPI for the API layer, PostgreSQL for transactional data, Redis for caching and job queues, Docker for containerization, and Kubernetes for production deployments.
mess_management_system_environments: The project maintains separate development, staging, and production environments. Staging mirrors production configuration as closely as possible and is used for release validation before each deployment window.
mess_management_system_release_process: Production releases are performed through the CI/CD pipeline after automated tests, security scans, and manual approval from the platform owner. Rollbacks are supported using the previous stable container image and database migration rollback scripts.
mess_management_system_monitoring: Operational monitoring for the Mess Management System includes application logs, API latency dashboards, database health alerts, and pod restart notifications. Critical alerts are routed to the on-call engineering channel.
